data.narrative:
Hexana is a Seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Sylvain Nizou and Paul Gauthe that has raised €25M to date. The valuation analysis is informed by a comp universe of 11 peers across nuclear energy—3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Nano Nuclear Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy—though the private nuclear energy subset lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables for robust peer-median benchmarking.

Given data constraints, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement. Using the €25M total raised as a valuation proxy, this approach yields an implied valuation of €62M. A sensitivity framework around this single method—incorporating downside and upside scenarios—produces a triangulated range of €53M (low), €62M (median), and €72M (high). The stage-progression result sits squarely within this band.

The primary limitation is the absence of a sufficiently dense peer cohort at the same stage and valuation tier. The nuclear energy sector remains fragmented across development phases and technology approaches, constraining cross-company comparability. A Seed valuation of €62M is defensible on stage mechanics alone, but this estimate should be revisited as additional private-market nuclear transactions and Hexana's own operational milestones emerge.
